title: Add Gemini CLI provider
description: Implement Gemini CLI as a first-class Relay provider using Gemini ACP, matching Claude and Codex managed-session support while preserving Relay’s provider-driven architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Managed Gemini sessions can be created, streamed, cancelled, resumed, revived, and lazily hydrated through Relay. Relay exposes Gemini models and runtime modes through provider capabilities, supports Gemini ask-user and plan-review flows, and can replay Gemini transcripts from canonical session storage. Tests and docs cover the rollout. Exact external Gemini session/process mapping may ship as a staged follow-up, but managed Gemini support must be production-ready.

title: Generalize provider runtime modes and interactive request payloads
description: Replace Relay's skipPermissions/planMode booleans and accept-or-decline request model with provider-defined runtime options and structured interactive request/response payloads that work across Claude, Codex, and Gemini.
acceptance_criteria: Core provider contracts let each provider declare runtime options through capabilities and send structured requests/responses for tool approvals, ask-user prompts, and plan-review flows. Claude and Codex continue to work without regressions, and managed-session persistence round-trips the richer runtime mode values.

title: Add Gemini ACP transport and managed session adapter
description: Build a thin in-repo ACP client over NDJSON and a Gemini provider session that spawns gemini --acp, manages lifecycle, streams output and activity, and bridges Gemini interactive requests into Relay.
acceptance_criteria: Relay can start Gemini ACP, initialize a session, create and load Gemini sessions, prompt, cancel, switch model and mode, surface permission requests, and capture the Gemini session id needed for managed restore.

title: Implement Gemini transcript replay and managed-session restore
description: Parse Gemini session JSON into Relay history and resolve Gemini session ids back to storage paths so managed Gemini chats can hydrate, revive, and rebuild state from canonical transcript files.
acceptance_criteria: Relay can replay Gemini transcripts into messages, thinking, tool activity, and stats; recover managed Gemini sessions after restart; lazy-hydrate Gemini chats from transcript storage; and preserve model/runtime metadata during restore.

title: Add Gemini model discovery and per-session sandbox switching
description: Expose Gemini models through Relay provider metadata with dynamic discovery plus fallback catalog, and let Relay change Gemini sandbox settings per session even if the Gemini process must restart and reload the same chat.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini models are available through provider-model APIs, auto-routing models are preserved, and changing Gemini sandbox mode from Relay updates the active session seamlessly without losing conversation state.

title: Make runtime controls and plan review provider-driven in the UI
description: Replace hardcoded permissions controls with provider-defined runtime pickers and route Gemini ask-user and plan-review flows through Relay's shared interaction UI without special-casing Gemini in the frontend.
acceptance_criteria: The chat composer renders runtime controls from provider capabilities, Claude and Codex behavior stays intact, and Gemini users can answer ask-user prompts and approve or reject plan-mode exits from the shared review flow.

title: Add external Gemini session discovery and exact process mapping
description: Discover Gemini sessions started outside Relay from Gemini storage and running processes, with reliable mapping between live Gemini processes and session files when multiple external sessions exist in the same repo.
acceptance_criteria: Relay can list historical external Gemini sessions from disk, identify active external Gemini sessions, and avoid misattributing concurrent Gemini processes in the same repo. Any remaining limitations are documented clearly.

title: Cover Gemini provider rollout with tests and docs
description: Add regression coverage and documentation for Gemini provider support, including ACP transport, transcript replay, runtime switching, sandbox behavior, shared UI changes, and rollout caveats.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests cover shared abstraction changes and Gemini-specific flows, relevant docs are updated to match the shipped behavior, and rollout caveats or staged external-session limitations are documented.

title: Redesign external session takeover UX in chat input area
description:
The chat input area for external (terminal-side) sessions has evolved incrementally and the current state is confusing:

**Current behavior:**
- User can type freely into the input area and press send — this triggers a takeover (converts external → managed session via --resume)
- We recently added a confirmation popup before the takeover happens, which helps but may not be enough
- Plan/build toggle and permission level controls are hidden entirely for external sessions
- Model/provider picker and reasoning level are shown but grayed out / disabled
- This creates confusion: users see a partially-functional input area and think things are broken

**Problems:**
1. The disabled controls with no explanation look like bugs, not intentional design
2. The full composer still invites typing even though the session isn't managed yet
3. The confirmation popup is easy to dismiss without reading
4. There's no clear visual signal that this is an "observe only" state vs an active session

**Possible direction:**
Replace the entire input area for external sessions with a simpler placeholder element — e.g. a card/banner explaining that this is a terminal session being observed, with an explicit "Take over session" button. This makes the state obvious and eliminates the confusing half-disabled controls.

**Process:**
Start by reviewing the current external session input area code and UX, discuss the specific pain points, and ideate on the right solution before implementing. This is a UX design task first, implementation second.

The rollout should preserve current Claude behavior while introducing provider-aware session creation, persistence, managed execution, and UI capability handling for Codex. This epic explicitly excludes Codex external-session discovery, transcript scanning from ~/.codex, and terminal/UI handoff parity with Claude.
acceptance_criteria: Codex can be used for managed sessions created and driven from the relay UI without regressing existing Claude flows; work is split into provider foundation, managed session adapter, managed-session persistence/history, UI capabilities, and docs/tests; Codex external session discovery is explicitly out of scope.

title: Make provider selection a first-class concept
description: Replace Claude-specific assumptions in core session creation and persistence with an explicit provider identity. Model this after t3code's separation between provider contracts and runtime orchestration: provider kind/config/session metadata should be explicit, provider-specific runtime details should sit behind a clean factory boundary, and the rest of the app should depend on normalized provider state instead of raw CLI quirks. This includes config/types for selecting a provider, provider-aware session metadata in the DB, and a clean factory boundary so InstanceManager does not hard-code Claude SDK vs Claude CLI selection.
acceptance_criteria: Instances can declare a provider kind; provider choice persists in SQLite; InstanceManager creates sessions through a provider-aware factory; existing Claude behavior remains default-compatible; no UI behavior changes required beyond plumbing.

title: Add managed Codex session adapter
description: Implement a ProviderSession for relay-managed Codex sessions using the local codex CLI. Heavily reference t3code's Codex architecture: keep the Codex-specific process/event handling isolated in its own runtime manager/adapter, translate raw Codex JSON events into a canonical relay event shape, and avoid leaking Codex CLI details across InstanceManager and the UI. The adapter should support first-turn creation with codex exec --json, subsequent turns with codex exec resume --json, model overrides where supported, interruption/close semantics, and translation of Codex JSON events into relay output/activity/status messages. Scope is limited to sessions created and driven from the relay UI.
acceptance_criteria: A managed Codex instance created from the relay UI can be sent multiple turns; output streams into the existing UI; session IDs are captured and reused for resume; unsupported capabilities are surfaced cleanly instead of pretending Claude parity; tests cover the Codex event-stream mapping.

title: Support managed Codex session restore and history replay

This includes persisting the provider/session metadata needed to resume managed Codex sessions after relay restarts and mapping saved Codex transcript events into relay history/state for those managed sessions only. External Codex session discovery and terminal-originated session import are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A relay-managed Codex session can survive relay restart with the right provider/session metadata; managed Codex history can be replayed into the UI as needed for restored sessions; no ~/.codex-wide discovery or import path is introduced.

Scope is limited to relay-managed Codex sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Users can choose Codex when creating a managed session; Claude-only controls or wording are hidden or adapted for Codex; provider-specific limitations are explicit in the UI; existing Claude UX stays intact.

title: VSCode icons and sidecar file icons
Surface provider usage status and rate limits
description:
Surface provider usage status and rate limits per provider in the UI. Goal: show users how much of their rate limit they've consumed and when it resets, so they can plan usage across sessions.

## Research Findings (2026-03-14)

### Claude (Agent SDK)

The SDK emits a `rate_limit_event` stream message on each turn with an `SDKRateLimitInfo` payload:

```typescript
// from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts
type SDKRateLimitInfo = {
  status: 'allowed' | 'allowed_warning' | 'rejected';
  resetsAt?: number;                    // epoch timestamp
  rateLimitType?: 'five_hour' | 'seven_day' | 'seven_day_opus' | 'seven_day_sonnet' | 'overage';
  utilization?: number;                 // 0-1 fraction — NOT sent for 'allowed' status
  overageStatus?: 'allowed' | 'allowed_warning' | 'rejected';
  overageResetsAt?: number;
  overageDisabledReason?: string;       // e.g. 'out_of_credits', 'org_level_disabled'
  isUsingOverage?: boolean;
  surpassedThreshold?: number;
};
```

**Observed payload** (Max plan, allowed status):
```json
{
  "type": "rate_limit_event",
  "rate_limit_info": {
    "status": "allowed",
    "resetsAt": 1773547200,
    "rateLimitType": "five_hour",
    "overageStatus": "allowed",
    "overageResetsAt": 1773540000,
    "isUsingOverage": false
  }
}
```

Key gap: `utilization` field is **absent** for `allowed` status. The type definition marks it optional. It likely only appears during `allowed_warning` or `rejected` states — but this is untested since we haven't hit those thresholds.

Currently discarded at `src/core/providers/claude-sdk.ts` in the `handleStreamMessage` switch (`case "rate_limit_event"`).

Also available but unused:
- `auth_status` stream event: `{ isAuthenticating, output[], error? }` — auth lifecycle, not rate limits
- `assistant.error` field: can be `'rate_limit'` (among others) — error state on assistant messages
- `system` subtype `api_error`: JSONL events with retry info — could surface transient rate limit 429s

### Codex (App-Server JSON-RPC)

**No proactive rate limit data available.** The app-server protocol has no usage, billing, or rate limit RPC methods or notifications.

What exists:
- `error` notification with `{ error: { message, codexErrorInfo? }, willRetry? }` — `codexErrorInfo` can be `UsageLimitExceeded` on turn failure
- `-32001` JSON-RPC error for server overload ("Server overloaded; retry later")
- `thread/tokenUsage/updated` — per-session cumulative token counts (already tracked in SessionStats)

What doesn't exist:
- No utilization/remaining/reset data
- No proactive notifications before hitting limits
- OpenAI API returns `x-ratelimit-*` HTTP headers on every response, but the app-server abstracts away the HTTP layer — headers are not exposed
- OpenAI has an admin Usage API (`/v1/organization/usage`) but it requires org admin API keys and only returns historical billing data, not real-time rate limit status
- Neither the Node nor Python OpenAI SDKs expose usage/billing resources

### CLI Provider (claude -p)

No rate limit events in the CLI JSONL stream. The CLI handles rate limits internally with retries. `api_error` system events may contain 429 errors but only surface as retry info.

### What `claude auth status --json` Returns

One-shot command (not a stream event): `loggedIn`, `authMethod`, `apiProvider`, `email`, `orgId`, `orgName`, `subscriptionType` (e.g. "max"). No usage data.

## What Was Attempted

Built full pipeline: `RateLimitInfo` type → provider adapters parsing events → `InstanceManager` aggregation → WS broadcast → sidebar UI with progress bars and token counts. Discarded because without utilization % or known caps, the UI could only show tokens used + reset countdown — which doesn't tell the user if they're at 10% or 90% of their limit.

## Blockers

1. **Claude SDK doesn't send `utilization` for `allowed` status** — the most critical field for showing "how much have I used" is absent in normal operation
2. **No way to know the user's plan token limit** — varies by plan (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise), not exposed anywhere
3. **Codex has zero rate limit data** — can only show error states after the fact
4. **No polling** — data only arrives when a managed session sends a message through relay. Usage outside relay is invisible.

## Possible Future Approaches

- **Wait for Claude SDK** to add `utilization` to `allowed` events (or file a feature request with Anthropic)
- **Warning-only mode**: Only surface rate limits when `allowed_warning` or `rejected` fires (skip the normal-state indicator). This may actually contain `utilization`. Needs testing by hitting actual limits.
- **Empirical cap detection**: Track the token count at which `allowed_warning` first fires, use that as the cap for future windows
- **Anthropic/OpenAI usage APIs**: Monitor for new first-party APIs that expose account usage
- **`claude auth status`**: Could use `subscriptionType` to look up published plan limits, but these change and aren't guaranteed accurate

title: Interactive plan document review UI
description:
Add an interactive review UI for **proposed plans** from the model — not finalized plans in the /plans route. When a model proposes a plan (e.g. via EnterPlanMode or a plan-formatted response), the plan should render as a rich in-chat UI (similar to how AskUserQuestion renders a custom card) with inline review capabilities.

## UX Flow

1. Model proposes a plan → renders as a custom card/component in the chat message flow (not a plain markdown block)
2. User can select text passages within the rendered plan and add inline comments — each comment is anchored to a specific selection
3. Comments accumulate visually (inline highlights + a comment list), each showing the quoted text + the user's note
4. User can edit/delete comments before submitting
5. On submit, all comments are combined into a single structured message (quoted selections + comments) and sent back to the model
6. Model responds with an updated plan and/or answers to questions
7. Could also support simple approve/reject without comments (like the existing permission banner pattern)

## Display Options

- **In-chat card**: Rich plan component inline in the message flow, similar to the AskUserQuestion UI or agent transcript cards. Comments appear as annotations on the card itself.
- **Wide drawer**: If the plan is long, could open in a side drawer (like the diff drawer pattern) for more reading room. Comments in a margin or overlay.
- Either way, this is part of the chat experience, not the /plans route.

## Implementation Considerations

- Proposed plans come through as assistant messages — need to detect plan-formatted content (ExitPlanMode tool use, or plan file content in the message)
- Text selection + anchoring: need to track selection ranges within rendered markdown
- Comment format sent to model: something like `> [quoted text]\n\nComment: [user note]` repeated for each comment
- Look at existing custom in-chat UIs for patterns: `AgentTranscript`, `AskUserQuestion` rendering in `claude-message.tsx`, permission banner
- The plan file at `~/.claude/plans/{slug}.md` is the source of truth — model updates it, we re-read
- Mobile: text selection is harder on touch, may need a simpler comment-only mode without selection anchoring

title: Interactive plan review UI with inline comments
description:
Add an interactive review UI for **proposed plans** from the model — not finalized plans in the /plans route. When a model proposes a plan (e.g. via EnterPlanMode or a plan-formatted response), the plan should render as a rich in-chat UI (similar to how AskUserQuestion renders a custom card) with inline review capabilities.

## UX Flow

1. Model proposes a plan → renders as a custom card/component in the chat message flow (not a plain markdown block)
2. User can select text passages within the rendered plan and add inline comments — each comment is anchored to a specific selection
3. Comments accumulate visually (inline highlights + a comment list), each showing the quoted text + the user's note
4. User can edit/delete comments before submitting
5. On submit, all comments are combined into a single structured message (quoted selections + comments) and sent back to the model
6. Model responds with an updated plan and/or answers to questions
7. Could also support simple approve/reject without comments (like the existing permission banner pattern)

## Display Options

- **In-chat card**: Rich plan component inline in the message flow, similar to the AskUserQuestion UI or agent transcript cards. Comments appear as annotations on the card itself.
- **Wide drawer**: If the plan is long, could open in a side drawer (like the diff drawer pattern) for more reading room. Comments in a margin or overlay.
- Either way, this is part of the chat experience, not the /plans route.

## Implementation Considerations

- Proposed plans come through as assistant messages — need to detect plan-formatted content (ExitPlanMode tool use, or plan file content in the message)
- Text selection + anchoring: need to track selection ranges within rendered markdown
- Comment format sent to model: something like > [quoted text] Comment: [user note] repeated for each comment
- Look at existing custom in-chat UIs for patterns: AgentTranscript, AskUserQuestion rendering in claude-message.tsx, permission banner
- The plan file at ~/.claude/plans/{slug}.md is the source of truth — model updates it, we re-read
- Mobile: text selection is harder on touch, may need a simpler comment-only mode without selection anchoring
close_reason: Implemented PlanReviewCard with text-selection-based inline commenting, replacing PlanApprovalContent

Investigate and improve session load performance
description:
Loading an individual session is noticeably slow. Initial app load taking a few seconds is acceptable, but navigating to a specific session should feel near-instant.

**Investigation scope:**
1. Profile and identify the current bottleneck — is it JSONL parsing, SQLite queries, WebSocket hydration, UI rendering, or a combination?
2. Measure where time is spent: server-side (history fetch, JSONL read/parse) vs client-side (message processing, rendering)
3. Check if we're doing redundant work (re-parsing JSONL that's already been parsed, re-fetching data we already have)

**Potential improvements to evaluate:**
- Pre-fetching: load session data in the background when hovering/navigating near a session, or eagerly fetch recent sessions on app load
- Data storage: cache parsed history in SQLite instead of re-parsing JSONL every time a session is opened
- Faster queries: optimize SQLite access patterns, batch reads, prepared statement reuse
- Incremental loading: show the last N messages immediately, lazy-load older history
- Client-side caching: keep previously-loaded sessions in memory so revisiting is instant

**Approach:**
Start by instrumenting the current flow to identify the actual bottleneck before optimizing. Don't assume — measure first.

title: Investigate slow chat loading for projects with many sessions
description: Chat loading is slow (~20-30s) specifically for projects with many sessions (200+). Server-side hydration is fast (0-84ms) and JSONL parsing is fast (5-30ms). The delay is between the server sending the WS response and the client processing it. Likely causes: (1) Multiple redundant WS subscribes per session — subscribe effect re-runs due to unstable function references from context re-renders triggered by instance_status floods. (2) Discovery poll blocks event loop for ~800ms every 10s. (3) Possible WS send buffer saturation from many instance_status broadcasts. Needs investigation with a production build (not dev mode) to isolate dev-mode artifacts (node --watch restarts, React strict mode double-effects) from real issues.
